newsitem.title: TUNISIA: Tunisia to cut money market rate next Tuesday.
newsitem.headline: Tunisia to cut money market rate next Tuesday.

text.p: The decision to cut average money market rate by 1.0 percentage announced on Thursday by Tunisian President Zine al-Abidine Ben Ali will come into force next Tuesday, a Central Bank source said on Friday.
"The decision announced by President Ben Ali will come into force next Tuesday, date of the next weekly auction called appel d'offres," the source said.
Bankers said that as a consequence, and starting next Tuesday, the money market rate (MMR) would fall to 7.81 percent from 8.81 percent.
They said MMR is set as an average between the two Central Bank refinancing rates, the appel d'offres and prise en pension rates.

Both are fixed by the Central Bank and maintain a fixed spread between them. Prise en pension is a seven-day repurchase facility at a punitive, higher interest rate, designed to provide banks with additional liquidity to that obtained through the appel d'offres.
The Appel d'offres rate has been 7.88 percent and the pension rate 8.88 since 1993.

Ben Ali on Thursday said that the decision to cut the money market rate was taken "considering the progress that has been made in containing inflation, and in the aim of providing eased conditions for financing and credit so as to stimulate investment and revitalize Tunisian businesses."

"This will make it possible gradually to achieve the desired flexibility of interest rates, as an instrument for the stabilisation of the money market and a factor of economic vitality," Ben Ali said in a speech.
Tunisia forecast an inflation rate of less than 4.5 percent this year after 6.2 percent in 1995.

Central Bank governor Mohamed Beji Hamda had earlier this year said in a report to Ben Ali that "efforts that should be made in relation to containment of inflation imply the interest rate playing a more active role in ensuring that the cost of money corresponds to its true price."
